dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Hey, did you know there's a lot of debate about whether Japan đầu hàng in World War II was because of the atomic bombs or not?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Of course I know! In Russia, textbooks teach that the Soviet Union entering the war was the main reason Nhật surrendered. The atomic bombs were just an excuse for America to show off its power.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: That's interesting. In America, we're always taught that the atomic bombs were the decisive factor. But recently many lịch sử scholars suggest that the Soviet Union declaring war on Nhật might have been more important.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Exactly! The Japanese had prepared mentally for civilian casualties, but they feared communism more than death. Lịch sử is always rewritten by the victors.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: You know so much about lịch sử. I like the way you look at issues from different perspectives. Maybe we should discuss this topic more over coffee?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Don't get ahead of yourself! I'm not easily swayed by compliments... but if you really want to learn more about the Russian perspective, maybe I could consider it. What do you think about the claim that lịch sử is just a propaganda tool?
